user_turns: Give me a quick health-check on my Klaviyo account — how many campaigns sent in the last 30 days, how many flows currently live, and roughly how many active profiles.
Drill into campaigns — which one generated the most attributed revenue over that 30-day window?
Which one generated the least, among campaigns that actually sent to a real audience (skip the test sends)?
Give me the subject lines for both of those.
Now switch to flows — which live flow generated the most revenue over the same 30 days?
How does that top flow's revenue compare to the top campaign's revenue from earlier? Which is bigger and by how much?
What are my 3 largest segments right now by profile count?
Of those 3, do any of them appear to overlap with the audience that the top-revenue flow is sending to?
Wrap this up as 3 bullet points I can paste into a CEO update — the health snapshot, the revenue winners, and one insight about audience/segment overlap.
judge_criteria: The final 3 bullets reference the specific top campaign and top flow identified in earlier turns — not new entities.
The 'revenue winners' bullet correctly identifies whether the top flow or top campaign was bigger (consistent with turn 7's comparison).
The audience/segment overlap insight references one of the 3 segments named in turn 8.
The health snapshot bullet includes the campaign-count, flow-count, and profile-count numbers from turn 1.
No metric, campaign, flow, or segment is fabricated in the final bullets — every claim traces to an earlier turn.
The final output is genuinely 3 bullets in a CEO-ready format (not a long prose dump or a rehash of every turn).
notes: 10-turn long conversation. This is the headline 'analyst standup' task — the kind of conversation a Klaviyo power user would have day-to-day. The synthesis at turn 10 requires referencing data from turns 1, 2, 5, 7, and 8. dtc-mcp's stateful sandbox lets the agent stash each piece in globalThis as it goes and assemble cleanly; klaviyo-mcp must either re-fetch (expensive) or rely on the LLM's working memory of earlier tool-result payloads (which may have been cache-compacted by turn 10). Strong expected gap.
